accuracy.evidence: Dates and facts checked against the expedition histories: Amundsen left Framheim 20 Oct 1911 and reached the Pole 14 Dec 1911 with dogs, skis and Inuit-style furs; Scott left Cape Evans 1 Nov 1911 and reached it 17 Jan 1912 (34 days later, so 'about 5 weeks'), found Polheim tent and flag, and all five died on the return. Endurance beset in the Weddell Sea Jan 1915, crushed and sank Nov 1915; camps on the floe; boats to Elephant Island; James Caird about 16 days to South Georgia; 36-hour crossing to Stromness; Yelcho reached the men on the fourth attempt on 30 Aug 1916; all 28 saved. Calendar model: day 0 = 20 Oct, 14 Dec = day 55, 1 Nov = day 12, 17 Jan = day 89, checked with POLEXART.DATE.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the mix-ups teachers report for this KS1 unit: that Scott won (race predict 'Scott, with ponies', challenge tag scott, p1), that ponies beat dogs on snow (kit predict, Ponies in deep snow card, tag ponies), that ice cannot break a ship (story predict, tags sailed/whale), that Shackleton reached the Pole or lost men (tags shack, half, none, m5), that brave means reckless (no-coat and run-off cards, tags nocoat/leave, p5) and North vs South Pole (tags north, desert, m1).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). 645 flagpolaran is about animal adaptations and 936 flagmidsun about day length; neither tells a human story. Here a calendar drag moves two sledges at their real paces (55 vs 77 days), the Endurance story is ordered from events, and the James Caird is sailed, the mountains climbed and the island rescued in sequence. The mechanics are tied to these expeditions' dates and route.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner drags the calendar and sees Amundsen's sledge reach the Pole on 14 December while Scott is still on the way, then Scott arrive on 17 January to a flag already there. Sorting kit makes them meet why dogs, skis and furs worked and ponies did not. Ordering seven story cards builds the Endurance narrative; the boat step makes them do the 16-day sail, the climb and the rescue in order (the island refuses a rescue before help is fetched). The brave/sensible sort separates courage from risk.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options that the lab disproves: 'Scott, with ponies' wins the race (the calendar shows Amundsen first), 'Ponies, they are bigger' pull better on snow (the kit card says ponies sink), 'No, the ship is too strong' (the story shows the ice crushing it). A fourth asks how many men got home with 'About half' and 'None' as tempting options; the rescue shows all 28. A.reveal reports each prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, each wrong answer tagged with feedback naming the slip: scott (second, 5 weeks later, found the flag), shack (never reached the Pole), ponies/cars (Amundsen used dogs), sailed/whale (sea ice crushed Endurance), half/none (all 28 home), nocoat/leave (brave is not careless), desert/north (South Pole is in Antarctica at the bottom). Wrong drops in the lab give the card's own reason, and the story and boat steps say what must come first.

readability.evidence: Kid text Flesch-Kincaid 2.3 (limit 6.5), adult 7.8 (limit 9.5). Short sentences and concrete words for ages 5–7; the two key words courage and endurance are defined in plain language. Canvas cards are one short phrase each; buttons say exactly what they do (Forward a week, Sail 4 days, Climb a mountain, Go to Elephant Island).

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and explanation similarity under 12% to every lesson. Each kid paragraph carries one part: where the Pole is, the race, Endurance, the rescue, what courage and endurance mean. Adult text gives curriculum fit, checked dates and the named mistakes with a note on telling Scott's ending gently.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 and desktop screenshots of every step after Show me (/workspace/wn-run-1116-0946/.tmp_run/shots). Text is scaled up for ages 5–7 (16 px banner, 17 px cards); sort boxes are about 170 × 100 px on a phone; story cards are 50 px tall in two columns; the calendar knob is 32 × 34 px with a 20 px larger hit band; the boat, mountains and island are large tap areas, and every action also has a full-width button.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five tasks complete with Show me, challenge shown, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes, no console errors. Every drag or tap has a button (Back/Forward a week, the two box names, each story card, Sail 4 days, Climb a mountain, Go to Elephant Island). The canvas aria-label reads the date and both teams' progress, the current card and boxes, the story so far or the boat's leg after every action, and messages are spoken with c.say.
